correctness.rationale: The proof reduces arbitrary positive-definite pullback forms to diagonal forms by averaging over the norm's coordinate sign isometries. Homogeneity gives a one-variable quotient. Its critical-point map is strictly decreasing because \(t^3+3t^2-5t+9=t(t-1)^2+5(t-3/5)^2+36/5>0\). Endpoint equalization at \(r_0=3^{-4/3}\), together with monotonicity in \(r\) on both sides of \(r_0\), gives the global minimax lower bound and matching upper bound. Numerical replay only checks the decimal evaluation.

value.rationale: The object is the canonical two-dimensional section of the classical Cesàro sequence space at the natural exponent \(p=3\). Because the norm is unconditional but not invariant under coordinate interchange, its exact Euclidean distortion is not a one-line symmetry consequence. The theorem gives a sharp algebraic contact parameter and an optimal pullback norm, providing a reproducible benchmark for the geometry of finite-dimensional Cesàro spaces.
